subject: Re: Clarify Exhibit E — pricing smoothing & packaging credits
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@velora.tech>

Cc: Velora Legal <legal@velora.tech>
Date: 2028-06-30T13:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify Exhibit E pricing smoothing + packaging credits

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the draft order form. A couple of points popped up in Exhibit E (pricing schedule) that Velora needs clarity on before we can finalize:

1) Pricing smoothing / true-up: the current language references both a quarterly true-up and an "annual cap" but doesn't define the look-back period or whether the cap is applied to a single true-up or aggregated annual exposure. Can you confirm the intended mechanics? Velora prefers a smoothing approach that won't trigger large retroactive charges during short-term usage spikes.

2) Packaging credits and SKU harmonization: Exhibit E ties packaging credits to committed SKU bands but also allows one-off surcharges for non-standard packaging. We need clarity on how those surcharges are invoiced and whether credits can be applied against them. If you expect monthly reconciliations, please confirm lead times and any maximum offset.

3) Escape hatch / exception handling: our procurement and finance teams asked whether there is a temporary "ramp" carveout for first 90 days post-launch (to account for unexpected product changes), and whether Redwood will accept a 20% cap on any single true-up charge during a ramp period.

Can you send a redline or short summary of how Redwood proposes to address these three items? If helpful we can jump on a quick call this week.

Thanks,

Samantha Lee
Head of Procurement
Velora Systems

Attachments: none

From: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify Exhibit E pricing smoothing + packaging credits

Hi Samantha — great questions. Short answers first, then attached is a consolidated redline and a scenario CSV that models the different true-up outcomes.

Summary (high level):
- True-up mechanics: Redwood's intent was a rolling two-quarter smoothing with an annualized true-up cap. Practically: monthly usage is reconciled each billing cycle, but invoice adjustments due to under-commit are batched into a two-quarter lookback to avoid single-month shocks. An annual cap of 25% (of committed spend) limits the cumulative adjustment in a 12-month window.

- Packaging credits: Credits are reconciled monthly and may be applied against packaging surcharges up to 100% of the surcharge in that month. If credits exceed surcharges, remaining credits roll forward for up to 6 months (deferred credit schedule). We can alternatively provide a one-time ramp credit applied in the first 3 invoices if Velora prefers simplicity.

- Ramp/escape hatch: We're open to a temporary ramp cap. Proposal: first 90 days post-launch, any single true-up charge is capped at 20% of the committed monthly fee; cumulative adjustments still subject to the 25% annual cap.

Next steps: attached "Velora_Redline_ExhibitE_v2.docx" includes tracked language for the pricing clauses and an appendix with the monthly reconciliation workflow. "pricing_matrix_scenarios.csv" models low/medium/high usage with and without the ramp carveout.

If this looks directionally OK, I'll loop in legal for precise language edits and produce a consolidated PDF for your counsel to review. Happy to take a 30-minute call if you'd like to walk through the CSV scenarios.

Best,

Priyom / Marissa / Karthik — quick legal pass on the proposed mechanics. Highlights and recommended language tweaks below (I'll add tracked changes in the doc):

- True-up cap wording: change "25% annual cap" to "25% annualized true-up cap with invoice adjustment look-back limited to 90 days for any single invoice adjustment." This narrows audit exposure and avoids multi-year retroactivity.

- Offset / clawback: do not use the term "clawback" without specifying offset mechanics. Recommend: "Any invoiced true-up may be offset against future invoices; Redwood may not seek direct repayment in cash for adjustments older than 90 days following delivery of supporting usage logs."

- Packaging credits: define timing and revenue recognition guardrails. Suggested: credits applied in the next invoice cycle, with a 6-month roll-forward expiration. If credits are material and affect revenue recognition, we should offer the one-time ramp credit as the default to simplify accounting.

- Audit and rights: add a 45-day notice window for usage disputes and the customer's obligation to provide supporting logs. Legal prefers the shorter dispute window to close out exposure.

- Force majeure / surge event carveouts: add specificity that "temporary production or supply-chain irregularities" do not automatically trigger a ramp carveout; carveouts require mutual written agreement and cannot be unilateral.

I'll insert these edits into Velora_Redline_ExhibitE_v2.docx and export a consolidated PDF (Consolidated_ExhibitE_markup.pdf) that we can share back. Also OK with the 90-day ramp cap proposal for the first 90 days but would like to convert any ongoing smoothing language into an explicit scheduling table to avoid ambiguity.

Lauren Bishop
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Samantha — attaching the consolidated markup with legal edits incorporated (Consolidated_ExhibitE_markup.pdf). Key points we updated based on our internal review:

- Converted the smoothing rules to a two-quarter batching model with an annualized true-up exposure capped at 25% of committed spend.
- For the 90-day ramp period we will apply a per-invoice cap of 20% on individual true-up adjustments.
- Packaging credits will reconcile monthly and may offset packaging surcharges; unused credits roll forward for up to 6 months. Alternatively, Velora may elect a one-time ramp credit in lieu of monthly credits.
- Legal added a 45-day dispute window and a 90-day look-back limitation for invoice adjustments; carveouts must be mutually agreed in writing.

Please review the attached PDF and let us know whether Velora Legal is comfortable with the revised language or if you'd like a short call to walk through the CSV scenarios. If we can get a sign-off by July 14 we can lock Q3 onboarding credits and the initial ramp credit we discussed.
